Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From e9e3d31d2c141af15518ce6578ef26480fe97878 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Brian Behlendorf <behlendorf1@llnl.gov>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2016 19:21:56 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] Allow 16M send/recv blocks

Fix an off by one error introduced by fcff0f3 which triggers an
assertion when 16M blocks are used with send/recv.  This fix was
intentionally not folder in to the Illumos commit so it can be
easily cherry-picked by upstream.

Signed-off-by: Brian Behlendorf <behlendorf1@llnl.gov>

diff --git a/module/zfs/bqueue.c b/module/zfs/bqueue.c
index 1ddc697b5..89655cf53 100644
--- a/module/zfs/bqueue.c
+++ b/module/zfs/bqueue.c
@@ -69,7 +69,7 @@ void
 bqueue_enqueue(bqueue_t *q, void *data, uint64_t item_size)
 {
 	ASSERT3U(item_size, >, 0);
-	ASSERT3U(item_size, <, q->bq_maxsize);
+	ASSERT3U(item_size, <=, q->bq_maxsize);
 	mutex_enter(&q->bq_lock);
 	obj2node(q, data)->bqn_size = item_size;
 	while (q->bq_size + item_size > q->bq_maxsize) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `module/zfs/bqueue.c`**
   - The assertion that checks the size of the item being enqueued has been modified. 
   - The original line:
     ```c
     ASSERT3U(item_size, <, q->bq_maxsize);
     ```
     has been changed to:
     ```c
     ASSERT3U(item_size, <=, q->bq_maxsize);
     ```
   - This change corrects an off-by-one error that was causing an assertion failure when using 16M blocks with send/recv operations.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `bqueue.c` directly addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (identified as `fcff0f3`). The bug was related to the handling of block sizes, specifically when the maximum block size was set to 16M. By changing the assertion from `<` to `<=`, the code now correctly allows for the maximum block size to be accepted without triggering an assertion failure, thus fixing the bug while maintaining the intended functionality of the queue.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
-	ASSERT3U(item_size, <, q->bq_maxsize);
```
Reason:
The assertion used a strict less-than comparison (`<`) instead of a less-than-or-equal-to comparison (`<=`). This caused an assertion failure when attempting to enqueue items that were exactly 16M in size, which is the maximum allowed size, thus preventing valid operations with maximum-sized blocks.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+	ASSERT3U(item_size, <=, q->bq_maxsize);
```
Reason:
The patch changes the assertion to a less-than-or-equal-to comparison (`<=`), allowing items that are exactly 16M in size to be enqueued without triggering an assertion failure, thus resolving the off-by-one error and enabling valid operations with maximum-sized blocks.
